newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian farm protests continue, talks bog down.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian farm protests continue, talks bog down.

text.p: Thousands of farmers blocked roads in Hungary for a second day on Tuesday while closed-door talks to end the protest over tax changes were reported to have bogged down.
Farmers driving tractors, ploughs, harvesters and occasionally family cars were out in bigger numbers than on Monday, the first day of the three-day protest, radio and media reports said.
Police said they had no overall figure for the number of protesters, but said that in some locations the turnout was smaller than on Monday. No violence was reported, police said.
The protests continued as a five-person government delegation led by Finance Ministry State Secretary Tibor Draskovics held closed-door talks with leaders of the protests by smallholder farmers.

The Hungarian MTI news agency said little had filtered out of the talks in the city of Kiskoros, central Hungary, adding: "All that is known at present is that, after more than an hour of negotiations, talks were still bogged down about the first point on the agenda.
"This point focuses on easing tax conditions of the agricultural producers, and the simplification of administration."
The farmers are protesting at the end of an exemption from social security contributions as of January 1 and new requirements to provide documentation for tax purposes.
The protest leaders have said they will end the road blockades on Wednesday but that protests could resume if the government does not meet their demands.

Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy, who did not attend the Kiskoros talks, said earlier the government was prepared to modify the new tax law but would not reinstate the social security exemptions for farmers or eliminate documentation requirements because this would create inequities in the system.
Farmers said they were increasingly frustrated by the government's position.

"If there is no agreement we are ready to continue our demonstration at any time because we have no choice and we have nothing to lose," Istvan Gargyan, a farmer from eastern Csongrad county, told MTI.
